news.title: Black Challenge Beat Defending Champions Turkey on Penalties to Reach 2026 Amputee World Cup Final
news.lede: Ghana’s Black Challenge have booked their place in the final of the 2026 Amputee World Cup after defeating defending champions Turkey 4-3 on penalties following a tense 1-1 draw in regulation time. The thrilling semi-final encounter saw the Ghanaian side demonstrate remarkable resilience and determination against the reigning champions, holding their nerve to secure a place in Sunday’s title decider. With neither side able to find a winner during regulation time, the contest was decided through a penalty shootout, where the Black Challenge converted four spot-kicks to overcome Turkey’s challenge. The victory represents a significant achievement for Ghana, who have now eliminated the defending champions to move within touching distance of the ultimate prize.

news.title: LIVE History is being written in Doha - Montenegro plays at the World Cup
news.lede: The Montenegrin cadet football team drew 1:1 with the Dominican Republic in the first, historic match of our selections at the world championships. "Sokolići" opened the match better and took the lead in the 12th minute. The scorer of Montenegro's first goal at the World Cup was Mark Đokaj, assisted by Petar Vujović. However, the Dominicans struck back through Camilo Castillo in the 24th minute.

news.title: Montenegro took the lead, was the better rival and stopped after conceding a goal: Cadet draw at the opening of the World Cup
news.lede: November 21, 2026 will be remembered as a historic day for Montenegrin football. For the first time, a team from our country participated in the World Cup. The cadet national team drew with the Dominican Republic at the opening match - 1:1. The first historic point at the World Cup was scored for our football team, but Radovan Kavaja's team could have won, especially in the first half, as they were a better opponent.

news.title: Serengeti Boys fight back to hold Costa Rica in World Cup opener
news.lede: Tanzania’s Under-17 national football team, the Serengeti Boys, made an impressive statement on their FIFA U-17 World Cup debut after recovering from a two-goal deficit to force a 2-2 draw against Costa Rica in their opening Group I match. Striker Faraji Kayanda emerged as Tanzania’s hero, scoring twice in the second half to rescue a valuable point for the debutants at Aspire Zone in Doha, Qatar. The result offered a strong response from head coach Elieneza Nsanganzelu’s youngsters, who looked in danger of suffering a difficult start to their maiden appearance at the global competition after conceding twice within the opening 15 minutes. Costa Rica took the lead in the eighth minute through Jefrey Urbina, who capitalised on an opportunity to put his side ahead and immediately increase the pressure on the Tanzanian youngsters.

news.title: Argentina wore borrowed yellow shirts in 1958 World Cup debut against West Germany
news.lede: Argentina opened their 1958 World Cup campaign in Malmö wearing yellow, after organizers decided their usual blue-and-white striped shirts could be confused with those of West Germany. The Argentine delegation had brought only that one kit, so stadium staff obtained a set of yellow shirts from local club IFK Malmö within a few hours. It was the only time Argentina wore yellow at a World Cup. According to the German Football Association, Argentina, listed as the away team, had to change.

news.title: Black Challenge to face Morocco in final of 2026 Amputee World Cup
news.lede: The Black Challenge held their nerve to secure a 4-3 win on penalties following a 1-1 draw after extra time, moving within one win of claiming their maiden world title. The two sides played out a goalless 50 minutes of regulation time before Ghana broke the deadlock nine minutes into extra time. Tournament top scorer Mohammed Mubarik converted from the penalty spot to give the Black Challenge the lead and take his tally to seven goals. Ghana’s advantage was short-lived, however, as Türkiye fought back to restore parity in extra time and force the match into a penalty shootout.
